According to arXiv 2501.19112, the AI Act handles contrary-to-duty obligations (CTDs) involving temporality by stating that there are cases where CTDs occur in combination with temporal constraints, indicating that a certain property used to be fulfilled but no longer is. An example provided is that if a notifying authority has sufficient reason to consider that a notified body no longer meets the requirements, the notifying authority shall investigate the matter with the utmost diligence.

To represent such cases, the suggested logic is temporal logic, which is a class of modal logics that can formally represent and reason with temporality. A popular system mentioned is Tense Logic (TL), which treats propositions as tensed and introduces temporal operators into the language, allowing for the representation of temporal relations.
